open_points.subject: R0-90 disclosure classification of a rule-breaking alias
open_points.text: “the alias is held as `business_confidential`, not `personal_data`” / “The customer's contact data and the object's address and identifying characteristics are `personal_data`”
open_points.question: When an alias contains a customer's name, contact data, address or another identifying characteristic, is its disclosure class determined permanently by the alias field or by the value it actually contains, and consequently do the no-agent, restriction and no-personal-data diagnostic guarantees still apply to that value?
options: The alias field is always `business_confidential`, even when its content is personal data
The actual content is `personal_data`, so it must not reach the agent or diagnostics
The field remains `business_confidential`, but specified additional controls apply when the writer breaches the rule
open_points.default_guess: Treat the field as statically `business_confidential`, because Registry explicitly does not inspect its content, and amend the semantic personal-data guarantees to state that limitation.

witness.initial: A restricted customer's phone number is entered verbatim as a project's alias.
events: The owner saves the alias; Registry accepts it because it is at most 40 characters.
The agent reads the project projection through Kernel.
outcomes: The agent receives the phone number because the alias field is classified `business_confidential`.
The read is refused or the alias is withheld because the value is customer contact data and restriction allows it to reach only the owner.

open_points.subject: R0-90 effect on the one-home and snapshot rule
open_points.text: “Registry's guarantees that no `personal_data` value reaches an agent and that no other service keeps one cover the values it holds in that class” / “Other services keep no customer record and no copy of these values”
open_points.question: Does R0-80 prohibit copies according to the actual value copied or only according to Registry's declared field class when a kept alias contains a name, address, tax id or other value R0-80 assigns exclusively to Registry?
options: The prohibition follows declared classes, so a snapshot may keep personal content placed in the alias
The prohibition follows actual values, so the consumer must not keep that alias content
A rule-breaking alias may be kept temporarily under an explicit remediation and retention rule
open_points.default_guess: Apply the prohibition by declared field class, as the changed passage states, but explicitly narrow R0-80 so it no longer claims that no other service keeps an actual copy of those values.

witness.initial: A project's alias is the object's full street address, and a consumer has no snapshot yet.
events: The consumer reads the project and stores the alias in its kept snapshot.
Registry continues to hold the same address on the project object as `personal_data`.
outcomes: The consumer keeps the address because it arrived in the `business_confidential` alias field.
The consumer must reject, omit or erase it because R0-80 says no other service keeps a copy of the object's address.
witness.observer: The consumer and the owner reviewing stored personal data

open_points.subject: R0-90 remediation of a rule-breaking alias already copied
open_points.text: “Registry promises nothing further about a value that breaks it.”
open_points.question: After the owner corrects a rule-breaking alias, what must happen to the old value already held in consumers' snapshots: must it be overwritten on the next read, actively invalidated or erased, or may it remain indefinitely?
options: The next successful project read must replace the stored alias
Registry or the owner must trigger invalidation or erasure in every consumer
Each consumer decides its own refresh and retention behavior, so the old alias may remain
No correction lifecycle exists; only anonymising or deleting the project removes the risk
open_points.default_guess: Require each consumer to overwrite the alias on its next successful project read, with no push invalidation by Registry.

witness.initial: A consumer snapshot contains an alias that names a person.
events: The owner corrects the project alias to a neutral label.
The consumer does not read the project again, or later performs an ordinary project read.
outcomes: The snapshot retains the person's name until the consumer independently discards it.
The old alias is erased immediately or is obligatorily replaced on the next read.
witness.observer: The customer, owner or auditor inspecting the consumer's stored snapshot
